facts.text: Grandview was originally part of the Cherokee Nation's lands, settled after the forced relocation of the Cherokee people during the Trail of Tears.
The Grand View School is a historic four-room stone schoolhouse built in 1938 by the Works Progress Administration during the Great Depression.
Grandview is located in the foothills of the Ozark Mountains, featuring rolling hills and timbered landscapes near the Illinois River.
Grandview has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild winters influenced by moist air from the Gulf of Mexico.
Non-Native settlers began arriving in the Grandview area illegally in the mid-1870s, drawn by opportunities in agriculture and trade.
Grandview is a rural community located near the center of Cherokee County on the northwest border of Tahlequah.
